text:
mira_pm: Quick sync — need to recalibrate RICE for the upcoming quarter. We got a few new enterprise asks (KMS audit, higher retention on logs) and a perf bucket (predictive batching). Do we shift weight from Reach -> Impact, or tighten Confidence gating?

alex.dev: My take: for Q3 we should upweight Impact. Reach estimates for infra features are noisy and bias product teams to UX work. Impact captures unit-cost wins and reliability.

sam_eng: +1 on Impact but we should also increase the minimum Confidence threshold for infra tickets to 60% so we don't overcommit.

lina_research: FWIW I ran a quick re-score for top 6 candidates using current weights (R:3, I:5, C:1, E:2). Results: Feature A (predictive batching): R=7 I=4 C=70 E=3 -> RICE calc -> `(7*4*0.7)/3 = 6.53` ; KMS audit automations: R=4 I=5 C=85 E=4 -> `(4*5*0.85)/4 = 4.25` ; Log retention opt-in: R=6 I=3 C=90 E=2 -> `(6*3*0.9)/2 = 8.1`.

mira_pm: Nice, Lina. If we change weights to (R:3, I:7, C:1, E:2) predictive batching becomes `(7*7*0.7)/3 = 11.43` which pushes it to the top. That feels OK given the cost/headroom numbers from infra.

alex.dev: That jump seems large — are we double counting cost savings as both Impact and Reach? Reach = number of requests affected, Impact = unit cost reduction. Those are orthogonal so it's fine, but be explicit in doc.

sam_eng: Also want to call out sequencing: predictive batching needs a small KV cache work first (dependency). If we punt KV cache it adds 2 sprints to ETA. So effective Effort changes.

jose_support: From customers: KMS audit and retention changes were asked by 3 paying customers, 2 on Dedicated. They tagged as blockers for contract renewal in 1 case. That should bump Confidence for those items (we can set C=95 for KMS).

lina_research: Updated scores with those inputs: KMS (R4 I5 C95 E4) -> `(4*5*0.95)/4 = 4.75`. Still below predictive batching with new weights.

mira_pm: So options: A) Move weights to (R3 I7 C1 E2) and prioritize predictive batching (but schedule KV cache prep first). B) Keep weights and prioritize log retention + KMS (safer for renewals). Which do we pick?

alex.dev: Vote: A but with guardrails — canary predictive batching with throttled rollout + auto-fallback. If telemetry shows regressions revert.

sam_eng: Vote: B. I worry engineering risk and unknown perf regressions.

jose_support: Vote: B if it secures renewals. If customers are at risk, fix that first.

lina_research: I'm neutral but will prepare an A/B rollout plan for A if we choose it. Also propose we create a mini-RICE for sequencing: score the dependency prep tasks separately and add them into pipeline.

mira_pm: Decision for today: We'll go with hybrid plan — prioritize KMS/retention for immediate enterprise risk (2-week scoped EPIC), AND start a 3-sprint prep lane for predictive batching (KV cache + smoke tests). Re-evaluate after the 2-week EPIC complete.

product-bot: New action created: `PRIOR-498` Owner: jose_support, Due: +10 business days -> "Enterprise retention + KMS audit triage".

mira_pm: Actions: 1) Jose to lead the enterprise EPIC, liaise with legal/security. 2) Sam to size KV cache prep (include perf tests). 3) Lina to run recalibrated RICE with updated E for KV prep and predictive batching. 4) Alex to draft canary rollback playbook.

sam_eng: I'll post infra ETA by EOD tomorrow.

jose_support: On it — looping in legal and infra now.

alex.dev: I'll start the canary PR template and share runbooks.

lina_research: I'll share a short doc with both sets of scores + a sensitivity table (Impact weight 5->7) so PMs can see breakpoints.

mira_pm: Great. We'll re-open this thread after the 2-week EPIC completes for final Q3 ordering. Thanks everyone :heart:

-- end thread --
